The flag of Israel is a horizontal rectangular flag with two indigo (dark blue or dark navy) stripes at the top and bottom, each occupying one-ninth of the flag's height, and a white stripe in the middle that occupies the remaining seven-ninths. In the center of the white stripe is a blue Star of David (Magen David), a six-pointed star that is a symbol of Judaism and, by extension, the Jewish people.

The colors of the flag are white, dark blue (indigo), and a specific shade of blue called "techelet," which is used for the Star of David. The blue used for the Star of David is a slightly lighter shade than the dark blue used for the stripes, creating a contrast that makes the star stand out prominently.

The design of the flag was inspired by a Jewish prayer shawl (tallit), which has white threads and blue stripes. The flag was officially adopted on October 28, 1948, shortly after the establishment of the State of Israel.
